name: jsdotnet
description: The jsdotnet plugin marketplace: the devbook knowledge convention and the delivery flow, as agents, skills, instruction files, and hooks authored once and read by both Claude Code and GitHub Copilot.

plugins.name: delivery
plugins.description: The host-neutral delivery engine: 16 flow-* staged procedures, 2 shared phases, 7 scheduled automations, and the pull-request lane, sequenced by the flow-runner agent through a closed set of extension points — spec, implement, verify, app.start, qa.run and deliver as services, session.start, flow.start, data.prepare, docs.update and flow.end as chores — with human gates a repository adds but never removes, and a run surface resolved from the live tool list so none is a normal outcome. Bindings, extensions, policy, and gates are declared per repository in .github/ai-agent-stack.json.

plugins.name: delivery-canvas
plugins.description: A render surface: a Mermaid diagram viewer and a Markdown document viewer, shown live beside the files they were written from. Implements one surface capability group — render (render_diagram, render_markdown) — with push/replace navigation and a history the Back button walks, as an MCP server for hosts that speak MCP and as two canvases for hosts with a canvas panel, from one copy of each page. Tracks no runs and exports nothing; declares no dependency and names no engine.

plugins.name: delivery-collector
plugins.description: A headless run surface: where a run becomes recorded rather than watched. An MCP server implementing two surface capability groups — lifecycle (open_dashboard, start_run, record_prompt, set_run_context, update_stage, finish_run, list_runs, get_run) and export (export_report) — keeping stage status, output, gate decisions, QA scenarios and the handoff marker on disk so a resumed session picks the run up where it stopped, and writing the run's Markdown report at the end. No page, no port, nothing rendered: the right surface for scheduled and unattended runs. Declares no dependency and names no engine.

plugins.name: delivery-dashboard
plugins.description: A run surface: the live dashboard a run is watched in. An MCP server implementing all three surface capability groups — lifecycle (open_dashboard, start_run, record_prompt, set_run_context, update_stage, finish_run, list_runs, get_run), render (render_diagram, render_markdown), and export (export_report) — with a run timeline carrying stage output, QA scenarios and their evidence, a Mermaid diagram viewer and a Markdown document viewer, and hook-captured tool and token telemetry. Rendered inline as an MCP App where the host supports it, served on 127.0.0.1 where it does not. Declares no dependency and names no engine.

plugins.name: devbook
plugins.description: The devbook convention: .arc42, .domain, .tech, .design, and .ai knowledge folders of addressed Markdown chapters, each carrying a parseable meta block with status ladders, a shared approved rung, runnable test-case links, and an opaque ext namespace a layered plugin keeps its own state in, compiled into derived _meta indexes and a reference-graph canvas. Ships per-folder orchestration skills, bidirectional to-spec-<kind> and from-spec-<kind> converters between chapters and code, a versioned contract with runnable migrations, and enforcement tooling.

plugins.name: devbook-collaboration
plugins.description: Review, comment, and hand-off workflows over devbook chapters. Requests a review and hands a chapter to a named reviewer, reviews one against its folder's rules and its evidence, records findings and the reviewer's verdict, runs the approval decision that writes devbook's own approved rung, and sweeps the adopted folders for what is awaiting whom and which approvals have gone stale. An L1 extension: every fact it remembers lives under ext.devbook-collaboration in the chapter's own meta block, so it adds no field to devbook's schema and needs no devbook release of its own.
